findings.detail: GPU-hours step rule divides the 229860 s budget by the checker's ratio-weighted (all tasks active) mean step, but the first 3/16 of the run is linear-only (~2.3 s vs ~11 s/step), so STEPS comes out ~10-15 % low and under-fills the matched budget. Use a two-phase formula S = (B - val) / (3/16*t_lin + 13/16*t_mix) or state the bias.

IN chain still emits --bn-recal-batches 0 --bn-recal-freeze true|false (and --bn-recal-validate at L1). Tested no-op, but the brief said scripts must not pass recal flags; drop them when BN_RECAL_BATCHES=0 or document the deviation in the report.

Claim that from-scratch L1 needs at most the final L1's memory is not established: the final L1 had frozen BN, while scratch trains BN at full resolution with 4 pairs (never run). Soften and list gpu_peak <= ~41500 MB explicitly for the scratch smoke.

Pre-change chain state files without group_args are assumed '--group-config B'; a chain started earlier with a different GROUP_ARGS would exit 2 on resume (fail-closed; no such chain exists). One line in the report suffices.

summary: The diff implements the agreed mapping (none = no group blocks; E = stem/encoder only with ungrouped linear reductions/dense_1 and deform decoder; B = both decoders; A = everywhere) through ModelConfig.group_encoder()/group_decoders(), so config.json and A/B graphs are unchanged; recorded full suite status 0 (1099 tests) and all three goldens 0 diff. Mixed configs across levels are rejected by existing equality checks and pinned by tests; streaming skips sums for ungrouped decoders (exact for none); IN needed no production change and is covered through AMP, cascade, L1 float32_fine (traced), streaming and predict with flip8/recenter; r_cascade.sh gains NORM with recorded group_args/norm, and r_level1_scratch.sh provides a resumable from-scratch L1 path with STEPS via env and the 63.85 h budget. Report has dry-run, smoke and long commands. Only NITs remain: the step rule under-fills the GPU-hours budget because it ignores the linear-only phase, the IN chain still passes no-op recal flags, the scratch-L1 memory claim is unproven, and old chain-state defaults need a note.
